subChunks.title: Defining Tables — CREATE TABLE and DROP TABLE
subChunks.hookHtml: Up to now you have queried existing tables. Now you will create them — defining the schema that everything else depends on.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
CREATE TABLE

CREATE TABLE spells (
  id          INTEGER      PRIMARY KEY,
  name        TEXT         NOT NULL,
  school      TEXT         NOT NULL,
  power_level INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  learned_by  INTEGER      REFERENCES apprentices(id)
);

Key column options

  • PRIMARY KEY — uniquely identifies each row; implicitly NOT NULL
  • NOT NULL — rejects NULL inserts for this column
  • UNIQUE — no two rows may share the same value (NULLs are typically exempt)
  • DEFAULT value — used when INSERT omits this column
  • REFERENCES table(col) — foreign key constraint

IF NOT EXISTS

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spells (...);

Safe to run multiple times — skips creation if the table already exists.

DROP TABLE

DROP TABLE spells;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS spells;  -- no error if absent

DROP TABLE is permanent and immediate. There is no undo unless you are inside a transaction. Add IF EXISTS to avoid errors in scripts.

AUTO_INCREMENT / SERIAL

-- MySQL:
id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY
-- PostgreSQL:
id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
-- SQLite:
id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY  -- auto-increments by default

storyBeats.text: Cipher hands you a blank ledger. 'Define the columns. The schema is your contract — change it later and everyone suffers.'

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: CREATE TABLE writes the schema into the archive. Every column needs a name and a type. Add NOT NULL for facts that must always be present. Add DEFAULT for values you want automatically. Add REFERENCES for foreign keys. And be careful with DROP — it destroys immediately, no questions asked.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 Create the spells table

Write a CREATE TABLE statement for a spells table with: id (INTEGER, primary key), name (TEXT, not null), school (TEXT, not null), power_level (INTEGER, not null, default 1).

guidedPracticeTests.label: Table created and INSERT works
guidedPracticeTests.overrideQuery: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spells (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, school TEXT NOT NULL, power_level INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1); INSERT INTO spells (id, name, school) VALUES (1, 'Fireball', 'Evocation'); SELECT * FROM spells WHERE id = 1;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the purpose of NOT NULL, DEFAULT, and REFERENCES constraints in CREATE TABLE. What happens at INSERT time when each is violated?

questions.prompt: What does `DEFAULT 1` in a column definition do?
options: Uses 1 as the column value if the INSERT statement omits that column
Requires all inserted values to be 1
Acts as a NOT NULL constraint
questions.answer: Uses 1 as the column value if the INSERT statement omits that column
questions.explanation: DEFAULT provides a fallback value. When an INSERT does not specify a value for that column, the default is used automatically.

questions.prompt: What happens when you INSERT a row without providing a value for a NOT NULL column that has no DEFAULT?
options: The INSERT is rejected with a constraint violation error
The row is inserted with a system-generated value
questions.answer: The INSERT is rejected with a constraint violation error
questions.explanation: NOT NULL with no DEFAULT means the column must always be provided. The database enforces this at INSERT time and rejects the statement if the column is omitted or explicitly set to NULL.

questions.prompt: What does `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS spells (...)` do when the spells table already exists?
options: Adds any new columns defined in the statement
questions.explanation: IF NOT EXISTS makes CREATE TABLE idempotent — safe to run in scripts that might execute multiple times without worrying about 'table already exists' errors.

questions.prompt: What is the danger of `DROP TABLE spells` without IF EXISTS?
options: If spells does not exist, the statement throws an error and can abort a script
It waits for all current queries to finish before dropping
questions.answer: If spells does not exist, the statement throws an error and can abort a script
questions.explanation: Without IF EXISTS, DROP TABLE on a non-existent table raises an error. In scripts, this error can abort the entire batch. Use IF EXISTS to make the drop safe regardless of whether the table exists.
